title: 2D Offset Pass starts at: rings stay at depth and link in the plane; lift only when an in-plane link hits the part or a fixture, with the reason named

body:
Part of #3741. Builds on #3744 (one ring set). Covers Inside and Outside (and Auto through #3744).

## The maintainer's words

"Simulation show that the path approach breaks down, instead of "going around the" object in the plane, it "lifts over" it picking up the contour ont he other side and starts ramping down back and forth to the desired depth again.. Where it should have just followed the contour keeping its plan not lifting the tool."

About Inside: "And it also does a shit ton of uncessary lifts.."

The rule from the #3741 comments: each ring goes around the part in the plane and stays at depth. Where a ring is split, the link stays in the plane when the path is clear. A lift is permitted only when an in-plane link would cut the part or a fixture. Then the status line names the reason.

## What happens

1. The 2D Offset uses `Links::PLANAR` (`crates/motion/src/links.rs:86-94`; `crates/app/src/operation/types/links.rs:65-67`). Its pass link is `Link::Retract`. `pass_link` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ladder_links.rs:154-225`) then lifts at every pass break, with no proof and no reason (`:161-163`, `:182`).
2. With `Link::KeepDown`, `link_proof` (`:243-261`) and, for a start side, `through_cut` (`:230-237`, `cleared_links` at `pocket.rs:346`) refuse a link between two Outside pieces that end on the part wall: the chord crosses the part.
3. The planner joins two pieces only when `linkable` (`level_order.rs:110-151`). Each other piece is a new pass, thus a lift.
4. After each lift the re-entry is the #3577 dead-end ramp (`ladder_links.rs:188-191`) or the #2265 solid restart (`:200-211`). This is the "ramping down back and forth".

Readings (synthetic dog-bone part, 80 x 50 stock box, D8, stepover 2, one level; see the #3741 research comment):

| Pass starts at | lifts (Retract) | re-entries | lifts (KeepDown) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outside | 14 | 13 | 14 |
| Inside | 8 | 7 | 7 |
| Auto | 7 | 6 | 7 |

The Outside counts are the same on `e313aa663` (#3353). #3577 changed only the kind of re-entry.

## Fix approach

1. With the one ring set of #3744, link ring k to the next ring at depth by a stepover link in the cut plane. The link runs through the band that the next ring cuts.
2. Make the in-plane link the rule for a start-side pass, whatever the pass link of `Links::PLANAR` is. A lift needs a reason.
3. Where the stock edge splits a ring, link the pieces in the plane through cut material or air when the chord clears the part and the fixtures.
4. Lift only when each in-plane link would hit the part or a fixture. Tally the reason with `st.tally.lift(why, ...)` and show it on the status line.
5. Check #3423 (P7, lifts between pieces) and close it as covered when this merges.

## Pins (red first)

- `start_side_rings_do_not_lift`: on a part with no split ring (a disc in a larger stock box), Inside and Outside have no lift and no re-entry on one level.
- `dogbone_start_side_lifts`: on the dog-bone part, count the lifts and re-entries of one level for Inside and for Outside. Each lift has a named reason in the notes. Expected: 0 lifts when each link clears the part.
- `lift_reason_is_named`: a fixture across the in-plane link gives one lift, and the status line names the fixture.

Effort `max`: a new linking law with a collision proof, under the safety floor.

Done means: the three pins are green, and the committed `testdata/models/fig8.step` with Inside and Outside has only lifts with a named reason.
